title: Stirred-Tank Bioreactors & Continuous Culture
topic: Simple vs Sparged Bioreactors, Dissolved Oxygen, Continuous vs Batch Systems, & Log Phase Maintenance
quickSummary: Bioreactors: Large-scale vessels (100–1000 L) providing optimal temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, and oxygen. Types: (1) Simple Stirred-Tank (curved base, motorized agitator, foam breaker); (2) Sparged Stirred-Tank (sparger ring bubbles air, dramatically increasing oxygen transfer surface area). Continuous culture drains spent medium while adding fresh medium to maintain cells in exponential Log phase.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Bioreactors scale up recombinant protein synthesis (100-1000 L) under tightly regulated physical parameters. Sparged stirred-tank reactors introduce a sparger ring to maximize oxygen transfer. Continuous culture systems replenish nutrients continuously to sustain cells in active exponential log phase.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Industrial Scale-Up & Bioreactor Systems
- Laboratory shake flasks produce limited yields ($<1\text{ Liter}$). Commercial recombinant protein production requires large specialized vessels called **Bioreactors** ($100\text{--}1000\text{ Liters}$ capacity).
- A bioreactor provides optimal growth conditions by continuously monitoring and regulating:
  1. **Temperature** (cooling/heating water jackets).
  2. **$\text{pH}$** (acid/base injection ports).
  3. **Substrate & Nutrient Feed**.
  4. **Dissolved Oxygen ($\text{DO}$)**.
  5. **Foam Accumulation** (mechanical foam breaker blades).

### 9.2 Bioreactor Typology: Simple vs. Sparged Stirred-Tank

| Feature | Simple Stirred-Tank Bioreactor | Sparged Stirred-Tank Bioreactor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vessel Design** | Cylindrical tank with a curved base to prevent dead zones | Cylindrical vessel with flat or curved base |
| **Agitation System** | Motorized flat-blade or marine impellers ensure even mixing | Impeller blades ensure homogenous nutrient distribution |
| **Aeration Mechanism** | Surface aeration and vortex air entrainment | Perforated **Sparger Ring** at the base injects millions of pressurized sterile air bubbles |
| **Oxygen Transfer Area** | Standard surface area | **Dramatically increased surface area for rapid oxygen dissolution** |

### 9.3 Continuous vs. Batch Fermentation Systems
- **Closed Batch Culture**: Nutrients are added only at the beginning. As cells grow, nutrients deplete and toxic secondary metabolites accumulate, driving cells into stationary and death phases.
- **Open Continuous Culture (Chemostat / Turbidostat)**:
  - Fresh sterile nutrient medium is continuously pumped in from one inlet port while spent medium and cells are drained at an identical flow rate from an outlet port.
  - This dynamic steady state maintains transformed cells in their physiologically most active **Log / Exponential Growth Phase**, producing significantly higher yields of recombinant biomass and active target proteins.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Fed-Batch Fermentation
conceptBreakdown.title: Fed-Batch Fermentation
conceptBreakdown.content: Fed-batch fermentation adds limiting nutrient feeds incrementally during fermentation to prevent substrate inhibition and catabolite repression without removing culture broth, achieving high cell densities.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Airlift Bioreactors
conceptBreakdown.title: Airlift Bioreactors
conceptBreakdown.content: Airlift bioreactors rely on rising gas bubbles inside an internal draft tube to drive fluid circulation without mechanical impellers, reducing hydrodynamic shear stress for fragile mammalian and plant cell cultures.
